citation: Tartarini and Schiavon (2020). pythermalcomfort: A Python package for thermal comfort research. SoftwareX 12, 100578. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2020.100578
description: pythermalcomfort is a Python package developed by Federico Tartarini, Stefano Schiavon and contributors for thermal-comfort, heat-stress and thermophysiological calculations. It implements PMV/PPD, adaptive comfort, SET, UTCI and other indices, with two-node and JOS-3 models for body-temperature responses. Inputs include air and radiant temperatures, humidity, air speed, clothing and activity, depending on the selected model. Outputs are comfort indices or physiological estimates for scalar or array inputs. Coverage is globally configurable at person or indoor-environment level, with temporal detail supplied by the user. Public source and package documentation are free under MIT, with Python 3.10 or later required. A limitation is that each underlying model has its own validity range and assumptions, so implementation of a standard does not establish applicability to every occupant. The package can evaluate comfort consequences of building-control simulations, complementary to EnergyPlus (model-energyplus). The README provides examples and the SoftwareX 2020 paper. No comfort calculation or physiological validation was performed.
